question: Does the coherent density floor run faster than G0, as its BPW implies?
answer: NO. 1.109x G0 GPU time while moving 17.4% fewer weight bytes.
harness: ascension_qwen38_hybrid_greedy --complete-wall --pairs 3, same binary, same prompt, each with its own uninstrumented generate_greedy control. timing_label DIRTY_ENGINEERING on both, so the COMPARISON is paired and the absolute is not offered.
verdict: If decode were bandwidth-bound, 17.4% fewer bytes would buy 17.4% less time: 23.976 ms. Measured 32.198 ms, 1.34x the prediction and 1.109x G0. The q3 codec's extra ALU per weight eats the whole byte saving and more. This is FINDING F2's ALU-issue bound showing up end to end: density only pays on this machine if decode cost per weight does not rise with it.
consequence_for_rans: F1 named interleaved rANS over the q3 body as the density route to 100 TPS, on a BYTES argument. rANS decode is MORE ALU per weight than q3 nibble unpacking, not less. G114-G116 must price decode ALU per weight BEFORE the byte saving or they repeat this result with a worse constant.

projection_refuted.why_wrong: The formula scales token time linearly in BPW, which assumes bandwidth-bound decode. Measured decode is ALU-issue bound, so every BPW-linear TPS projection in this campaign inherits the error.
